owner_note_occurrences.text: The first verse in the epistle of Jude gives us insight into this process. This letter is addressed “to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called.” That word called is better read as invited. This word is quite different from how it is used in Matthew 22:14, where Christ says that “many are called, but few are chosen.” This is God personally inviting someone to be part of His Family. And this verse shows that before God calls an individual, God the Father sanctifies him or her.

style_policies.title: Reverential capitalization of pronouns referring to God the Father and Jesus Christ

owner_note_occurrences.text:
Please use Reverential Capitalization Style Many modern Christian publishers and specific translations (like the New King James Version or New American Standard Bible) use "reverential capitalization," where any pronoun referring to deity is capitalized. If you are using this style, you should capitalize the pronouns referring to God the Father and Jesus:

- he becomes He (referring to God)
- me becomes Me (referring to Jesus)
- him becomes Him (referring to God)

Here is how the verse looks with reverential capitalization applied:

John 8:29 And He that sent Me is with Me: the Father hath not left Me alone; for I do always those things that please Him.

Reverential Capitalization in the Grow Daily (GD) Translation Throughout this text, pronouns referring to the Father and the Son are capitalized. When Christ refers to Himself with a capitalized Me or My, it does not imply a lack of humility in His spoken words, but rather reflects the typographic reverence of the translation itself. It also acts as a visual guide to help readers track who is acting or speaking in pronoun-dense verses, making daily reading and study clearer.

This rule should be last because in case i find out it’s not appropriate, then I can always modify the rule, I just want it to be easy to revert to when the reverential capitalization happened. I just need to confirm if when referring to self is appropriate. I will have it changed regardless but I want it last so it’s easier to get it back to before that last change. The reason, I want a full edited Bible before I get a minister to look at it.
